column1: # Every JavaScript file git tracks, with the reason it cannot be Elm or Haskell (ADR 0007).
# `just js-check` (marola-tools js-check) fails on a file that is not here and on an entry that matches
# no file, so this list only shrinks. An entry ending in / covers a vendored folder. <path><TAB><reason>.
# The new site: glue around libraries and browser APIs Elm has no binding for.

column2: the JavaScript side of Elm's two ports: starts the page and carries out the effects Elm cannot (MapLibre, geolocation, localStorage, history, the document's lang, alert)
MapLibre GL JS is a JavaScript library with no Elm binding: its map, markers, popups, sources, layers and camera calls live here, string in, string out
the wind and wave particles are a MapLibre custom layer: a WebGL program MapLibre calls every frame, which Elm cannot be
Vite, which bundles the compiled Elm with ports.js, reads its configuration only as JavaScript
vendored third-party code, unchanged: MapLibre GL JS and PMTiles, with their licences
runs the built page (compiled Elm is JavaScript) in a stub DOM and a MapLibre stub; testing a JavaScript bundle needs a JavaScript engine
calls @protomaps/basemaps' layers(), a JavaScript-only package, to write front/public/map/style.json; by hand, with the network, never at build time
